newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh govt forecasts grain harvest at 15-16 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh govt forecasts grain harvest at 15-16 mln T.

text.p: Kazakhstan's government expects this year's grain harvest to total 15-16 million tonnes, but the agriculture ministry believes output will only be 13-14 million tonnes, an agriculture ministry spokesman said.
The economy ministry gave a higher figure of 16.5 million tonnes in July, revised down from 18 million tonnes.
Last year's disastrous drought-hit grain harvest totalled about 10 million tonnes.
"This year we can realistically expect 13-14 million tonnes, but it all depends on how the harvest finishes," the agriculture ministry spokesman, Alexander Korablin, told Reuters.
He said Kazakhstan's annual domestic demand for grain was about eight million tonnes, comprising 4-6 million tonnes for fodder and 2.8 million tonnes of food grain.
The balance is mostly exported to traditional markets in other former Soviet republics, mainly Russia, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan.
Korablin said Azerbaijan was also interested in buying Kazakh grain, but he could give no details.

He said the final outcome of the harvest will depend largely on weather in the coming weeks. "We can expect the rain to turn to snow at the end of September, then there will be a brief window for harvesting in October before more rain and snow."
Kazakhstan has sown 17.12 million ha of grain this year, including about 12 million ha of wheat.
Drought hit some Western areas, where 900,000 ha were written off. The harvest had been completed in the west and south.
